goals: Use grid search and random search with cross-validation
why: Default settings are rarely optimal. Sensible tuning of, say, tree depth or learning rate is often a cheap accuracy gain, and a badly tuned model can look worse than it is.
explain: **Parameters** are learned from data (regression coefficients, split thresholds). **Hyperparameters** are chosen by you before training (max_depth, k in k-NN, learning rate).
**Grid search** tries every combination from a list. It is thorough but explodes combinatorially: 5 values × 5 values × 5 values = 125 models × 5 folds.
**Random search** samples combinations at random. With the same budget it usually finds equally good settings, because only a few hyperparameters really matter.
**Bayesian optimisation** (Optuna, Hyperopt) learns from previous trials which regions look promising. It is the standard for expensive models like XGBoost.

example.title: Tuning a random forest
steps: Retrain on the full training set, report test F1 once = 0.80
example.result: Test ≈ CV confirms the tuning did not overfit the validation folds.

mistakes: Huge grids over hyperparameters that barely matter.
Forgetting to fix random seeds when comparing.
takeaways: Hyperparameters are set by you; parameters are learned
Always tune with cross-validation, and test once

practice.code:
from sklearn.datasets import load_breast_cancer
from sklearn.model_selection import RandomizedSearchCV
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
X, y = load_breast_cancer(return_X_y=True)
search = RandomizedSearchCV(RandomForestClassifier(random_state=0),
    {"n_estimators": [100, 200, 400], "max_depth": [3, 5, 10, None], "min_samples_leaf": [1, 3, 5]},
    n_iter=8, cv=5, scoring="f1", random_state=0).fit(X, y)
print(search.best_params_, round(search.best_score_, 3))

check.why: Set before training; the others are learned.

check.q: With a fixed budget, random search often beats grid search because…
options: It explores more distinct values of the hyperparameters that matter
check.why: Grids waste trials repeating values of unimportant hyperparameters.
